- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days), especially after recent spikes.
- Model overestimates prices in the middle to late horizon (days 10–25), particularly when history shows recent volatility or downward momentum.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — forecasts remain high longer than actuals.
- After sharp price spikes, model overshoots and fails to correct quickly, leading to overprediction in subsequent days.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to pull prices back toward historical averages when volatility subsides.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent low prices, often underreacting to rebounding trends.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating short-term reversals or sudden spikes.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model overestimates continuation, ignoring potential reversal signals.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market events (e.g., auction results, regulatory changes) in the short term.
